title: Evolution cannot have found optimal solutions to complex fitness constraints

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Evolution cannot have found optimal solutions to complex fitness constraints

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Since iterative random search converges only for simple constraints, the roughly trillion generations of life on Earth are insufficient to find optimal solutions to complex constraints, so most features of organisms are merely good-enough solutions rather than optima.

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: it is still completely implausible that the trillion or so generations of organisms since the beginning of life on Earth would be sufficient to allow optimal solutions to be found to constraints of any significant complexity.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci A New Kind of Science claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Stephen Wolfram, A New Kind of Science (Champaign, IL: Wolfram Media, 2002), Chapter 8, “Implications for Everyday Systems”; section “Fundamental Issues in Biology” (from p. 383), p. 386. Scope: biological evolution as an iterative random search

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on wolfram2002-ch08-10: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.35

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Empirical fitness landscapes can test optimization claims for proteins and laboratory systems. They do not span organismal features, deep time, or the full adaptive history, and complexity lacks one accepted metric. Existing data therefore resolve proxies and restricted cases only.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: For traits with measurable fitness landscapes, compare observed phenotypes with global optima and simulate evolutionary search under reconstructed mutation, population, and generation counts. Widespread optimality on demonstrably complex landscapes would refute the claim; persistent suboptimality would support only restricted versions.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Global biological fitness is environment-dependent and multidimensional.

Available fitness landscapes cover tiny molecular subsets and few generations.

Present suboptimality does not identify search-time insufficiency as its cause.

fields.value:

discriminating power: 0.28

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Search cost on hard discrete constraints can be measured, and a trillion evaluations is a concrete budget for a simulation study of modest landscapes. Organismal fitness landscapes for complex traits are not a public dataset, so the conclusion that most features are merely good enough is not resolved by the computational analogy. The claim splits into a testable search statement and an unmeasured biological inference.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Run iterative random search for a fixed budget of about 10^12 evaluations on constraint landscapes graded by complexity, and compare the residual to the optimum. Rapid success only on simple landscapes would support the computational half. Calling organismal traits good enough rather than optimal further requires a measured fitness landscape, which this budget alone does not supply.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Biological search is not a uniform random walk: recombination, population structure, and developmental bias change the effective budget.

Significant complexity and good enough are not defined for real organisms.

data adequacy: 0.3
operationalizability: 0.45
analysis feasibility: 0.45
